prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1168; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed the first notice of loss for a left-turn collision at an intersection. Insured reports the other vehicle came through on the oncoming side while the insured was turning. Police report requested. No injuries reported at the scene by either driver.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel, who requested that all contact go through the firm. Acknowledgment letter sent to counsel's office confirming receipt of the bodily injury claim. Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash, treating with a primary care physician.

Entry 3: Received the police report. Citing officer documented the claimant's vehicle as stopped in the oncoming lane before the collision. Insured's statement and the report are not fully consistent on signal phase. Flagged for liability review and possible scene photos from the intersection camera.

Entry 4: Medical records requested from the treating provider under the signed authorization included in counsel's letter. Records show initial complaints of neck pain, range-of-motion limitation, and a diagnosis of cervical strain. Follow-up scheduled for physical therapy. Reserve reviewed and adjusted pending records.

Entry 5: Spoke with defense counsel regarding comparative fault. Liability currently assessed as shared, leaning toward the insured based on the left-turn yield requirement. Settlement evaluation deferred until treatment is complete and the physical therapy discharge summary is received.
